However, there IS a separate, genuinely unrelated project called 'Chain Games' with ticker $CHAIN (different ticker, similar 'Chain' branding) that can cause name-based confusion in searches; and the asset itself has gone through two identity changes (CHN->XCN ticker swap, then Chain->Onyx protocol/brand rename), which is why confidence is 'medium' rather than 'high' despite Upbit's Korean/English names ('오닉스코인'/Onyxcoin) matching the current official branding exactly.
XCN.rebrand_or_token_swap_history: Significant, well-documented rebrand chain: the project began as 'Chain' (Chain.com), with a token called CHN. In March 2022 CHN was rebranded/converted to ticker XCN at a 1:1000 ratio (per Bittrex Global's official announcement and CoinCarp). In 2023, a governance vote (CIP-007) renamed 'Chain Protocol'/'Chain DAO' to 'Onyx Protocol'/'Onyx DAO' while KEEPING the same XCN ticker/token unchanged in function -- so Upbit's 'Onyxcoin' name reflects the 2023 rebrand of the same underlying XCN asset, not a different coin.

XLM.notes: CoinGecko and stellar.org confirm XLM (Lumen) is Stellar's native asset. CoinGecko search for 'XLM' returns only this one project.

XPL.chain_or_platform: Plasma (own EVM-compatible L1, backed by Tether, focused on stablecoin payments)
XPL.notes: CoinGecko and plasma.to confirm XPL is Plasma's native L1 asset, matching Upbit's '플라즈마'/Plasma. CoinGecko search for 'XPL' also lists 'Wrapped XPL' (WXPL, a bridged representation of the same asset -- not a collision) AND a separate, apparently unrelated project literally called 'Pulse' using the exact same ticker XPL -- genuine ticker collision risk flagged.

XRP.notes: CoinGecko and xrpl.org confirm XRP is the native asset of the XRP Ledger (distinct from the Ripple company). CoinGecko search for 'XRP' returns only this one project.
